---
title: "Memory Palace: Hierarchical Retrieval for LLM Memory Systems"
subtitle: "Context-Efficient RAG with Verification Tokens for Hallucination Prevention"
abstract: |
  Large Language Models suffer from context window limitations and hallucination when
  retrieving from large knowledge bases. Standard RAG architectures use flat vector
  search, loading excessive context that increases latency and cost while providing
  no verification of factual grounding. We present Memory Palace, a hierarchical
  retrieval system that organizes knowledge into domain-indexed tiers with multi-hop
  retrieval. Our approach introduces: (1) hierarchical domain routing that reduces
  context by 97% compared to flat RAG, (2) embedded verification tokens enabling
  hallucination detection with F1=0.92 at near-zero compute cost, and (3) SMASHIN
  SCOPE encoding for structured, retrievable memories. We evaluate against BEIR
  benchmarks (Natural Questions, HotpotQA, MS MARCO) and compare with ColBERT,
  Contriever, and GraphRAG. Results show Memory Palace achieves 56% average NDCG@10
  while using 97% less context, with built-in hallucination prevention that
  outperforms SelfCheckGPT and FActScore.
---
